resale_co.name: Certificate of Continuing Occupancy (CCO / Certificate of Occupancy for resale)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Palisades Park Building Department (Construction Official as Enforcement Officer)
resale_co.lead_time: Ordinance: inspection within a reasonable time, not exceeding 30 days after the application is complete.
requirements: General inspection of the visible parts of the building before a sold or vacated home is occupied
Smoke detector installed as required by state law before the CCO can be issued
Certificate of Smoke Detector, Carbon Monoxide Detector and Fire Extinguisher Compliance from the Bureau of Fire Prevention

Office checklist: all permits finalized, no open building code or property maintenance violations, egress, handrails on stairs with 3 or more risers, extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen, working windows, no keyed locks on interior doors, no trash accumulation
Notarized Residential Owner Certificate with purchaser's affidavit on the number of dwelling units (LLCs must name the manager/principal)
If the home is being used as an illegal 3+ family, separate utility services for the illegal units must be removed and owner and buyer must sign a sworn statement

fees.label: Residential Owner Certificate form fee, one to two unit dwellings (form dated 06-21-2023)
Reinspection per unit (form dated 06-21-2023)
fees.quote: $50.00 REINSPECTION FEE PER UNIT FOR EACH ADDITIONAL INSPECTION

resale_co.how_to_apply: Get the Residential Owner Certificate (Resale) application from the Building Department or the Borough's Applications, Forms and Permits page, have the purchaser sign the affidavit before a notary, and pay the fee to the Borough of Palisades Park. An inspection is scheduled after payment; if it passes the CCO is issued at the inspection. File the separate smoke/CO/extinguisher application with the Bureau of Fire Prevention.

evidence.quote: The BOROUGH OF PALISADES PARK does require a Certificate of Occupancy (CO) for resale of a property in conjunction with a Certificate of Smoke Detector, Carbon Monoxide Detector, and Fire Extinguisher Compliance.
After paying the appropriate fee, an inspection is scheduled and conducted. If the inspection is satisfactory, the CCO is issued at the inspection.
Prior to any rental, lease or sale of any building or any portion thereof, the owner thereof shall apply to the Enforcement Officer on an appropriate form for a certificate of continuing occupancy.

No certificate of continuing occupancy may be issued to a residential building or any portion thereof unless an approved smoke detector device has been installed as required by applicable state statute and local ordinance.
*APPLICATION MUST CONTAIN PURCHASERS ORIGINAL SIGNATURES AND BE NOTARIZED

resale_co.notes: Chapter 198 of the Borough code requires a certificate of continuing occupancy before a sold residential building is occupied, and the Building Department FAQ confirms a CO is required for resale together with the smoke/CO/extinguisher certificate. The fee amounts conflict: the code (Section 198-9, last amended 2009) lists $50 one-family, $75 two-family, $25 zoning review and $15 reinspection, while the Borough's Residential Owner Certificate form (dated 06-21-2023, scanned image PDF) charges $150.00 for one to two unit dwellings and $50.00 per reinspection. The form is the more current document; confirm with the office. No validity period is published.

requirements: Smoke detectors on each level and within 10 feet of sleeping areas (110V with battery backup and interconnected in homes built after 1990); detectors over 10 years old must be replaced
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of all sleeping areas; detectors over 5 years old must be replaced (per the Borough form)
All smoke and CO alarms in working order
Fire extinguisher of the correct size, properly mounted, within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)

authorities.name: Palisades Park Bureau of Fire Prevention

fees.label: Smoke detector and CO alarm compliance certificate, per dwelling unit per inspection
fees.quote: The fee for smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm compliance as aforesaid shall be $100 per dwelling unit per inspection.

authorities.how_to_apply: Submit the Bureau's 'Application and Certification in Lieu of Inspection for Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Portable Fire Extinguisher Compliance' (all boxes must be checked; owner, agent, tenant or NJ licensed electrician certifies) to the Bureau at 275 Broad Ave, with the closing date and contact person. Office hours Monday to Friday, 9:00 A.M. to 4:00 P.M.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official (Chief Fire Inspector: Michael Valente)

evidence.quote: Before any Use Group R-3 or R-4 structure is sold, leased or otherwise made subject to a change of occupancy for residential purposes, the owner shall obtain a certificate of smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm compliance (CSDCMAC), evidencing compliance with N J.A.C. 5:70-4.19, from the Bureau of Fire Prevention.
The fee for smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm compliance as aforesaid shall be $100 per dwelling unit per inspection.

Our typical responsibilities consist of the performance of periodic and follow-on fire inspections, responding to complaints, fire investigations, smoke detector and carbon monoxide compliance, and public education and awareness.
APPLICATION AND CERTIFICATION IN LIEU OF INSPECTION FOR CERTIFICATE OF SMOKE DETECTOR AND CARBON MONOXIDE ALARM AND PORTABLE FIRE EXTINGUISHER COMPLIANCE

fire_cert.notes: Borough Code Section 143-34 requires the CSDCMAC from the Bureau of Fire Prevention before a one- or two-family home is sold, and Section 143-38 sets $100 per dwelling unit per inspection (no tiered rush fees published). The Bureau's form is titled a certification 'in lieu of inspection', so it is unclear whether an on-site inspection is always done. The form still lists a portable fire extinguisher, which P.L.2025, c.19 removed from the sale certificate in February 2025. The form is a scanned image PDF.

other_items.label: Open permits and violations
other_items.detail: The resale inspection checklist requires all permits to be finalized and no outstanding building code or property maintenance violations.

other_items.label: Illegal extra units
other_items.detail: If the inspection shows the home is being used as a 3+ family in violation of zoning, the separate utilities for the illegal units must be removed and owner and buyer must sign a sworn statement before the CCO.

open_questions: Which resale CCO fee is current for a one- or two-family home: the code's $50 / $75 (2009) or the form's $150.00 (06-21-2023)?
Does the Bureau of Fire Prevention accept the 'certification in lieu of inspection' for home sales, or always inspect, and is the $100 fee charged either way?
Is a fire extinguisher still required for resale after P.L.2025, c.19?
How long is the CCO valid, and how much lead time does the Building Department need?
